speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My Ministerial Statement today will address the 25 oral and written questions that were filed for the Parliament Sittings in July.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the last 12 to 18 months, we spent some time closely evaluating the performance of the Sports Hub project, including its performance in the pre-COVID-19 period, with a view to assessing if we should continue with the partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We took a holistic long-term look at the changing environment in the sporting, lifestyle and also entertainment ecosystem in Singapore and what we wanted to achieve in our sporting and social policy outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A main consideration was our desire to bring stronger community participation and activities to the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Once we reached that view, a detailed financial, legal and operational due diligence was carried out with the support of external consultants and advisors to satisfy ourselves that taking over the Sports Hub would indeed be a viable option.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Thereafter, we engaged with SHPL to inform them of our decision and worked through the details of the handover.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will organise my response along the following lines: first, set out the historical and contextual reasons leading to the development of the Sports Hub via a PPP – I will explain why we chose the PPP model for this case; second, explain the changed environment and the reasons which led to the termination of the partnership as well as the details around the termination, including the financial information; finally, I will touch on what we envisage for the community and Singapore following the change of ownership and management of the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Prior to the development of the Sports Hub, the former National Stadium stood in the same location.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was officially opened in 1973 and hosted its first major event in September that year – the seventh Southeast Asian Peninsular Games – the SEAP Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was a place where major national, sports and entertainment events were held, such as the Malaysia Cup – which Members, I am sure, will recall – where the stadium echoed with the "Kallang Roar" and concerts by global stars like Michael Jackson, Stevie Wonder, Bon Jovi and Mariah Carey.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am not sure if this is all in our generation but I am sure you recall.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also hosted 18 National Day Parades before the last in 2007.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The report recommended that the National Stadium be redeveloped into a multiuse Sports Hub with top-tier infrastructural facilities for both sporting as well as lifestyle and entertainment activities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This would give us a world-class venue that could compete with the world's best in attracting major sporting and entertainment events into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This would in turn also help in the larger development of our sports and lifestyle entertainment industry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Following the report, the Government commissioned an in-depth feasibility study.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It then announced plans in 2003 for the redevelopment of the former National Stadium into the Sports Hub that we see today to achieve the outcomes stated in the Sporting Singapore Report.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Sports Hub was to be a new best-in-class international stadium envisioned to bring our sports, social and lifestyle offerings to the next level and position Singapore as a leading venue for local, regional and international events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With this in mind, the Government had to decide on the best way to design, finance, build and operate the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Broadly, there were two options available to us at that point in time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under this model, the Government fully finances the upfront capital investment for the project and thereafter either pays a service provider to run the project or does it on its own.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government would also bear the costs and risks of undertaking the project from the start, including the design and construction and in also getting suitable parties to come in to operate the project.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under this arrangement, the Government could tap into current international private sector expertise, particularly where the project was innovative and cutting edge, as the Sports Hub was intended to be.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A suitable partner would fully undertake the design, the construction as well as the financing of the operations and management of the project and thus, in this way, also directly bear the risks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government would not have to incur any upfront capital costs or financial outlay until the project was completed or operational.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Thereafter, the Government would then commit a steady stream of payments to the private sector partner for the entire duration of the project term.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Given the unprecedented scale and complexity of such a major sports infrastructural project in Singapore and the limitations at that time of not having sufficient depth and breadth of such expertise in Singapore, including in the private sector, we chose to adopt the PPP model.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These reasons have previously been fully explained in this House but let me briefly emphasise a few points in relation to the choice of the PPP model for this project to address the various questions raised by hon Members.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, as I said earlier, the PPP approach allowed us to benefit from the expertise of major international private sector partners with worldwide experience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Sports Hub development as an integrated sports, entertainment and lifestyle hub was to be the first of its kind in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In terms of infrastructure, it was to be a new innovative, forward-looking world-class sports facility that was intended to be configured for different events, be it sports, entertainment or lifestyle.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a global events venue, it had to be able to attract live entertainment events from all over the world as well as provide a first-class spectatorship experience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At that time, neither the Government nor our local sporting or lifestyle entertainment industries had sufficiently matured and developed depth of experience, networks and contacts in bringing in marquee sports and entertainment events from all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Thus, besides needing to tap on market leading experts with not only the right technical expertise to build the infrastructure, we also needed the experience and connections of someone with international sporting and entertainment networks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Based on our assessment, SHPL was chosen as the PPP partner because each of the consortium members of SHPL brought with them substantial expertise that was relevant to certain key aspects of the project.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, InfraRed Capital Partners for project financing; Dragages Singapore to design and build the project; Cushman & Wakefield for the subsequent facilities management; and Spectra for the venue operations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we also wanted to ensure that our partners would have skin in the game.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The PPP model was useful for this because it allowed risks to be shared with the private sector in two material ways.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I would illustrate this by outlining the terms of our own PPP with SHPL.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, as I mentioned earlier, there is no upfront cost to the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The entire project design, planning and construction were borne by the PPP partners, from the time the project started in 2010.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government did not pay any of the upfront construction costs at all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These annual payments go towards SHPL's debt service repayments for the loan they took out to finance the Sports Hub construction, as well as day-to-day maintenance and operations of the asset.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are payments which we would have had to make, had the Government chosen to undertake the project on our own.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These payments were also subjected to and moderated by SHPL's achievement of a broad and comprehensive range of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) which were set out expressly in the project agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These KPIs included the availability of Sports Hub facilities and performance of services, such as events and activity programming, infrastructure maintenance, cleanliness, estate management, security and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Overall, having no upfront costs for the Government turned out to be useful.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, when the Global Financial Crisis in 2008 hit unexpectedly, as the Government's fiscal resources were not tied up, we were able to use those resources to meet other pressing economic and other needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, this structure also allowed the Government to mitigate the, sometimes, unexpected risks of such a major project undertaking.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, these risks did come to bear.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SHPL also bore the costs of addressing the defects such as the roof leaks, the inadequacy of the pitch and poor sound quality for concerts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In all of these cases, whether in delay to the project, or to the cost of rectifying the project, the associated costs were borne by SHPL because, under the PPP, it assumed the risks for both timing and quality.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, the PPP structure ensured that there would be inherent financial discipline in the project.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I explained earlier, this was a ground-breaking, novel project and we had not undertaken such a project, at least on this scale before.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As such, this was an effective incentive built into the PPP model to ensure that they align and maintain commercial discipline and minimise the risks of any budget overrun.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was essentially a project that had two parts: the design and building of a world-class sporting, entertainment infrastructure, or the hardware – which took place at the outset – and the subsequent running and operations of the project to meet sporting, lifestyle and community aspirations, spread over about two decades.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On the infrastructure, it is vital that we get it right, from the get-go, from the start.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It would be difficult, if not impossible, to change the hardware mid-stream, or once it is built.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we needed the relevant expertise to achieve this, to get it right, build a world-class cutting-edge facility.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As to the operations and running, I have explained how the consortium's know-how and networks and connections were key to the initial periods, when international marquee events were attracted to the Sports Hub in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This reserves to the Government the right to assess, at any time, if its interests might be better served by stepping in to run the Sports Hub directly – run, own and manage, directly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If so, there is an agreed mechanism upfront, right at the start of the arrangement, for such a mechanism and there is a clear formula that defines what happens consequent to that decision.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Overall, this structure enabled the Government to manage its interests, through the different phases of this project, to mitigate its financial risks, to drive greater economic efficiency and also align the parties, particularly in relation to the upfront design and construction of the new infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Leong Mun Wai, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Ms Sylvia Lim, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Sharael Taha asked about the roles of SHPL and the Government in the PPP; what the arrangement entailed; the ways in which SHPL had fallen short; and the reasons why the Government decided to terminate the PPP.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The current arrangement has helped us achieve the world-class sporting infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, it has really been about five, five and a half years, with another 13 years to run.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In terms of getting a world-class sporting infrastructure, I have explained that and I think we have achieved that.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When we set out to redevelop the former National Stadium, the intent was to have a Sports Hub capable of staging major events and entertainment events of world standards.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And through the PPP, which has worked well, we now have a world-class Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It has won international accolades for its architectural design, hosted multiple major international events such as the International Champions Cup, HSBC Rugby 7s and also, more in line with today's concert-goers – BTS, U2 and Coldplay.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members in this House know that there were some early infrastructural problems that occurred after operations began, such as the roof, the pitch, the lights and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When these occurred, we imposed the suitable and relevant financial penalties to hold them accountable.,By and large, SHPL made efforts to work with SportSG to correct them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, when it came to promoting and enhancing the vibrancy of community sports and lifestyle activities at the Sports Hub, the project did not do so well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We wanted to see SHPL invest in the creation of their own new event intellectual properties and building on existing event properties, but these did not come to fruition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But it is also an iconic national sporting asset and there must be a strong sense of affinity and connection between Singaporeans and the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There ought to have been more community participation and activation around the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, we would have liked to see the sporting community from the grassroots, from schools and junior national athletes, having more access to the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hosting National School Games – key events like the finals – could be at the Sports Hub, or grassroot programmes and activities, family days or carnivals around sporting or social objectives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are programmes for which there will not likely be any or much commercial return.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our assessment is that this would be difficult to change by just adjusting some KPIs or trying to improve the outcomes with SHPL via negotiation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We had in fact tried this for some time, but the difficulty lies in the inherent structure of the project terms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, SportSG had wanted to bring in ActiveSG academy programmes such as the Basketball Academy at the OCBC Arena but encountered resistance as such programmes were not revenue generating.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The costs of hosting school sport events, such as combined sports days and National School Games, were also high and in some cases, prohibitive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Due to SHPL's exclusive subcontracting arrangement with its catering subcontractor, community events organisers that wanted to cater for their own food and drinks also had to pay high levies for doing so.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These costs were then either borne by the event organisers or passed on to participants.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A number of Members – Mr Darryl David, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Shawn Huang, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Gerald Giam and Dr Wan Rizal – asked about the Government's vision and plans for the Sports Hub moving forward, after we take over and how it would benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Besides what I have already outlined, let me share a few ideas which SportSG and other agencies are already working on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As an over-arching consideration, the Sports Hub will be made more accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to make it a community icon that Singaporeans can identify with and feel a part of in their social and sporting activities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are thus planning regular Sports Hub and National Stadium Open Houses with activities for the young and the old, and of course, everyone else in between.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, as part of our Unleash the Roar! national project, children who have joined our new ActiveSG Football Academies can also participate in the year-end football tournament at the National Stadium.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are also working with MOE to host even more National School Games, such as the Track and Field, Netball and Rugby competitions, as well as the Singapore Youth Festival performances, or even some Sports Days for schools, at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our children can then aspire to play and compete at the National Stadium, or simply come, soak in the atmosphere and cheer on their schoolmates.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The plans for the National Day Parade for the next few years are not out yet, but regardless, the Sports Hub will be a place where all of us – both young and old – will be able to build treasured memories and meaningful shared experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Seniors from all walks of life can also participate in mass events such as GetActive!

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singapore at community spaces in and around the Sports Hub, including the 100PLUS Promenade, OCBC Square and the nice space along the waterfront.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also hope to see the return of the casual stroller or jogger to the stadium, by enhancing access to the stadium.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Where community programmes such as ActiveSG events and activities are concerned, we will also aim to keep them affordable and accessible to all and we will ensure that as many community spaces as possible are open and free for all to use.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Therefore, the second key reason for the taking over the Sports Hub is to achieve greater integration with the broader Kallang Alive plans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This picture provides an overview of the future Kallang Alive Precinct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As part of the Kallang Alive Precinct plan, there will be an expansion of sporting facilities around the Sports Hub, which will be developed, owned and operated by SportSG directly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Here, we see the ongoing construction and an artist’s illustration of what it will look like when completed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of these that I have just shown are assets which sit outside the current Sports Hub group of assets.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They are part of the Kallang Alive Precinct but not within Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are also other facilities, such as the Youth Hub, in the longer-term pipeline with youth-centric activities and "young" and "youth" here include those who are young at heart as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Once ready, these entertainment and lifestyle offerings will integrate with and support the activities of the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are exciting plans which we have in store for the future.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have a vision to transform the entire Kallang Alive Precinct, including the Sports Hub, into one single integrated ecosystem which is not only capable of hosting world-class events, but also to be the home ground for our national athletes as they train and compete.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We want this to be the beating heart of our community, grassroots and school sports and the testbed and breeding ground for sports innovation and growth.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Taking over ownership and management of the Sports Hub will enable SportSG to unlock the Sports Hub’s full potential for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will integrate the Sports Hub more closely with its upcoming facilities within the precinct to deliver more seamless offerings and capture stronger precinct synergies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members might ask, what does this integration entail and what does this mean?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, integration from a physical perspective, which will allow us to do more with one event.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members would have seen a glimpse of this at the recently-concluded WTT Grand Smash earlier this year, where we had table tennis tables set up around the main event, which the public could use to play with family and friends while they waited for the elite matches, and these were matches that were taking place with some of the world's best and we had tables around to engage the community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: People come freely and play while waiting, engaging the entire community in the precinct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With the fuller integration with Kallang Alive and the upcoming facilities, we can step up on this and activate more of the Kallang precinct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: High-quality international marquee events will be complemented side by side with local programming.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We can use the entire spread, all 89 hectares of the Kallang Alive Precinct seamlessly to do so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By concurrently integrating community programming on the sidelines and in the months running up to the event, many more Singaporeans can benefit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These could include community tennis for the masses to try out the sport, tennis clinics for social competitive players and aspiring athletes, youth competitions and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we will have a whole ecosystem of sports – our professional athletes competing in the arena, our budding young athletes training on the sidelines and in the facilities, and the general public enjoying a social game, all integrated with the other lifestyle offerings which will be coming up.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It will also provide for better and dedicated experiences for participants and audiences.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, integration from a user point of view.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With different ownership structures and different commercial profit and loss, it can be incredibly challenging to achieve seamless integration in the delivery of services across the entire suite of facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, adversarial competition between the facilities is the more likely outcome.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, by taking over the Sports Hub, we will be able to give users a more integrated service experience across the entire precinct, for instance, precinct-wide promotional and marketing activities and hospitality offerings that span across multiple facilities and programming.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Beyond just integrated service experiences, users are likely to enjoy cheaper costs as SportSG will now be able to reap precinct-wide economies of scale through shared functions and services.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Overall, taking back the Sports Hub and integrating it with Kallang Alive will enable us to unlock greater value and achieve our broader social and sporting vision for the wider precinct as a whole.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I spoke a little bit about this earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One of the key reasons for working with SHPL and choosing them as a partner was to rely on their expertise and networks with many other networks and international players around the world.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over the years, our own sector in Singapore has grown and matured and we are now much better placed to continue making Sports Hub a premier hub for sports and entertainment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over the past few years, SportSG had played a key role alongside SHPL to bring in major sporting events, such as the WTA Finals, International Champions Cup and Rugby Sevens and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have developed the know-how, links, networks and the experience to continue doing this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Besides that, our local and locally-based companies have also matured.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Companies, such as UnUsual Limited and LiveNation, are now much more established and can bring in larger gigs into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Group One Holdings and Ironman Asia have also continued to grow, introducing several flagship events that Singaporeans can identify closely with and actively participate in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our growing capabilities and international recognition as a premier hub for sports and entertainment can be seen in major names that have set up operations in Singapore as well, such as AEG and IMG, as well as NBA which has announced the set-up of their Singapore office.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Third, demand for these events has also grown.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With our recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic, there is now greater demand and we see that gradually ramping up, both locally and regionally, for larger-scale sport, lifestyle and entertainment events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Overall, the limitations of the current arrangements, the changing environment and our growing capabilities and ambitions are all factors that we considered when deciding on terminating the relationship.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members Mr Edward Chia and Mr Sharael Taha asked about the impact which the termination in this case might have on the guidelines and considerations for future PPPs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this case, we foresaw in this arrangement that it was long term, that circumstances could change along the way and we provided upfront for an agreed no-fault termination without penalty in the PPP.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have outlined above, we had good reasons to terminate the PPP, with regard to the reasons I have outlined.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But having reached this decision does not necessarily mean in all cases, that the Government should no longer be open to other PPP projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Regardless of how projects are financed, we have a sound evaluation process to review the business case, scope, lifecycle cost, implementation approach and also the relative risks between Government and private sector for each of these projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For PPPs, in particular, a framework is in place to assess the suitability of undertaking the PPP, including tangible outcomes, potential for downstream lifecycle cost savings, the nature of project risks, which will differ from industry to industry and project to project, the available private sector expertise in that area relative to what the Government can offer and the need for flexibility or the likelihood of downstream changes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of these are factors to be taken into account and I would say that no two projects would be similar.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having explained the reasons for termination, let me turn now to explain the costs of termination and how it might compare with carrying on with the PPP project till its conclusion in 2035.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Edward Chia, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Ms Sylvia Lim, Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas have all asked about the costs of termination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: How does it compare with what we would pay if we had continued with the partnership till 2035?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And if it is different, how do we account for it?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To do so, let me just quickly recap a few financial points on the PPP which I had raised earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, SHPL funded the full initial capital expenditure for the construction of the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They did so by taking out a loan.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This meant that the Government did not have to contribute any upfront capital for the construction in 2010.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we did not pay upfront and it is also now that the cost of the loan for the financing of the infrastructure, the capital cost, is still being borne by SHPL.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Third, with this fee from the Government, SHPL would then be responsible for the full operating expenditure, including daily operations, maintenance, security and lifecycle costs for the entire project term.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Fourth, the assets would be returned to the Government at no cost in 2035.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This sum does not take into account net present value and other financial or accounting adjustments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With the termination, the Government would have to pay two main buckets of costs and let me explain them to Members.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first is the amount to be paid to SHPL for the termination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This amount is made up of several components, derived from the financial terms stipulated in the Project Agreement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I had explained earlier that this Project Agreement contemplated this early termination on a no-fault basis without penalties and the agreement itself provides for the formula by which such a termination sum can be calculated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, the $1.2 billion or so of the sum that would be paid will go towards the capital expenditure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I explained earlier, this is the capital expenditure that the Government would have had to bear if it adopted the traditional procurement approach of proceeding with the Sports Hub on its own.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The remaining components, or about $300 million, are due to the fair market value of the Sports Hub, which is commercially negotiated and also other costs, expenses and deductions, based on the Project Agreement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the final amount will be based on the accounts as at the date of handover, which is December.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there could be some fluctuations and variations, but we do not expect there to be material variance from this figure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second bucket of costs is the costs of the future running and operating of the Sports Hub, post-handover.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, for parity of consideration, let me sketch out what this cost is projected to be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Sharael Taha asked about this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will take, as a benchmark, the current operating assumptions and costs incurred by SHPL which include, as I mentioned earlier, maintenance, operations, security, future lifecycle costs, replacement, programming costs, day-to-day costs and so on, all the way until 2035, which is the comparable period.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Based on this, and we use data from actual incurred, that means, this is from SHPL's actual incurred, we expect to incur approximately $68 million per year doing this for operations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is roughly the same, although I have not gone into the decimal places.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The termination sum, added to the projected cost of maintenance and operations, is roughly comparable to what it would cost had we chosen to continue with the PPP and incurred the availability payments over the rest of the project period until 2035.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, with the component figures taken at face value – and as I have said, without taking into account accounting and other net present value adjustments – this aggregate sum would be comparable to the financial obligation committed under the PPP if we had chosen to continue with it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Taking the two buckets of costs to be paid for the termination – the sum to be paid to SHPL, which largely reflects the upfront capital expenditure and future operating costs – this would be a fair deal for the Government on which to take back the assets.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: None of these components are penalties to the Government, as I have said, because the project agreement provides for a no-fault termination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Indeed, we do not plan to operate the Sports Hub at status quo or on the same assumptions as SHPL.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As you heard me say earlier, we want to make the Sports Hub more accessible, invite more participation, bring more people into the Sports Hub, make it more accessible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To do this, we would have to have more community programmes, invest to bring more world-class events into the Sports Hub and open up the Sports Hub and the National Stadium to general community use.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of this would probably mean higher expenditures and increases in daily operating and maintenance costs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As such, we should probably expect our operating expenditure on an ongoing basis, once we take over, to likely be higher than what it was previously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the same time, however, this might be balanced off against the future revenue generated by the events and activities at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Previously, under the PPP, any revenue that was generated by these commercial activities would go into the project.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When we run it, albeit we want to do it in a different way on different assumptions, the revenue that we generate will go back directly to mitigating and defraying any of the increased costs in maintenance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The PPP project has enabled us to have a strong foundation of a world-class infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We intend to build on that and continue to bring in top-tier international sporting and entertainment events whilst, at the same time, incorporating our ambition of attaining wider and better social and sporting outcomes for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This structure will enable SportSG to focus on the Sports Hub, but also, at the same time, have regard to the wider Kallang Alive Precinct and what could be done in those cases, when the other projects that I have mentioned in the Kallang Alive precinct come onstream.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where necessary, it can be operated as a single, integrated entity, able to reap synergies and economies of scale across the entire suite of sporting and lifestyle assets of Kallang Alive.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A team of officers from SportSG has already been earmarked to move into the Sports Hub holding company and manage Sports Hub on a full-time basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are officers who have had years of experience with the Sports Hub, many of them having worked alongside SHPL since the inception of the project in 2014, gaining experience and know-how along the way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These officers within SportSG have already been functionally organised in a structure that coheres with the structure of SHPL, suited to running the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They have been in this position for the last few years, readying for a takeover if and when needed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Beyond the internal capabilities of SportSG, we value the expertise and experience of existing SHPL employees and would like to retain them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Beyond the internal structure and resources, we intend to continue working and partnering the best providers in the private sector in the areas of programming, broadcast, hospitality, facilities upkeep and management, to name a few.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will, therefore, continue to retain the contracting model.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, the model where we can subcontract and work with external parties in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This allows us to work with market-leading, optimal partners to provide the best services and facilities fit for the particular purpose in question, for a particular occasion or event.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the mid to longer term, we also intend to tap into the private sector, to explore the prospects of redeveloping some parts of the Kallang Alive precinct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, projects, such as the redevelopment of the Kallang Theatre into an integrated multi-purpose sport, entertainment and lifestyle hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Or even turn the Kallang Wave Mall into a one-stop sporting, health and wellness destination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Then, at that time, we had the "Pesta Sukan Minggu Merdeka" or Sports Festival Week of Independence, which was an annual feature in our National Day celebrations from 1966 to the early 1970s.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This was an event which was not just about excellence in high performance sports, but really, sports for all, as part of our culture and in our everyday life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As then-Minister for Social Affairs, Encik Othman Wok, put it in his speech at the ground breaking of the former National Stadium in 1966, he says and I quote, "Sport… must be an essential feature of our way of life.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The new generation will not fear stagnant thinking because they will have dynamic reflexes built into them".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We must go back to that spirit and conviction to make sports an essential feature of our everyday life, because of the impact it can make in our own lives and in the lives of others around us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of my own fondest memories growing up were the excitement of being able to play at the Zone or National Finals at the old National Stadium, or simply being in the stands, skipping class, supporting and cheering my friends as they competed against rival schools.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It made me feel like I was part of something bigger, larger, something more.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it connected me with my school, friends and, certainly, with the sport in a way which no other way can – intangible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sport has this immense power to bind us as one, to be hungry for more and to strive to be the very best.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is what our TeamSG athletes embody when they compete under the Singapore flag and it is the spirit that we want to see in every Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Together, sport can make us more resilient individuals and strengthen our sense of unity as One Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the heart of it, this next chapter of Sports Hub is about sports being a part of the life or everyday life of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As we close the previous chapter, let me also acknowledge SHPL for its contributions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Sports Hub will be a place where our students grow to be resilient, as they deal with wins or losses in their school colours; where we bond with our family and friends, as we enjoy running around the jogging track, participating in the community sports events and enjoying international concerts.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have a clarification that is linked to an oral Parliamentary Question (PQ) which I filed previously.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Minister talked about going beyond sports and about involving the community a lot more in the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had the privilege of  marching in the PCF contingent for the only NDP held at the Sports Hub since – I think it was in 2016 – and I can say it was a wonderful experience.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, Minister, in the past, as you know, the NDP would be held one year at the old National Stadium; one year at the Padang.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to perhaps commit to a more regular schedule of having the parade held at the Stadium, at the Sports Hub and perhaps even involving the Kallang Alive area, in a month of celebrations, say, across the entire month of August, that leads into a meaningful celebration at the NDP?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I am glad that he enjoyed marching in the PCF contingent.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I am very glad to hear about the move and I have a clarification for the Minister about the leadership of the Sports Hub going forward, starting with the CEO.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I think we will need a CEO going forward who is able to understand the vision, execute on the vision and really bring it alive.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And importantly, a CEO who is able to build the leadership team to help him or her to achieve all of this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I do not want to go into specifics at this point in time, but I agree with Mr Xie Yao Quan that we do have to look out for qualities, such as an ability to integrate with the rest of Kallang Alive.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is, after all, one of the fundamental raison d'être behind why we are doing this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That person must have strong organisational skills because they are several components that come together that are not just sports, but also lifestyle, entertainment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You have got to deal with the local ecosystem, have an eye for who our best international and private sector partners might be, liaise with them externally, bring in international events into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And there must, most importantly, also have a clear eye on being able to use the Sports Hub's assets to be able to drive our sporting, social and lifestyle outcomes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And those are the key qualities that we will look out for, for the leadership of Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am heartened to hear from the Minister that once the Government takes over the Sports Hub's management, we are going to do a lot more things for a lot more Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But, Sir, that will also mean that we need a lot more resources.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Bearing in mind that the MCCY budget is always amongst the smallest in every Budget, I would like to ask the Minister whether he can go to the Finance Minister and ask for more funding because, Sir, especially when we celebrate National Day next week, the lion must roar.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Before we embark on this, we satisfied ourselves that at least for the baseline of what we say we want to achieve, we have enough resources to drive towards.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, obviously, the details as to what an enhanced budget might look like is something we will have to discuss closely.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we have to bear in mind our current fiscal constraints and position as well.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, will the Sports Hub and Kallang Alive precinct be used to host all national sports competitions and national school games and can SportSG make greater efforts to market such events to a wider audience?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will inspire our young athletes to push themselves harder, increase the public attendance at such competitions and also free up other community sports facilities to the general public.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These facilities, as some might be aware, tend to be blocked booked by the National Sports Associations for competitions and training, to the consternation of some members of the public.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the first point, yes, it would have been possible to work with third parties and private sector partners in the traditional procurement model.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Indeed, that is the case in many procurement models.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the reasons I outlined earlier carefully about the unique nature of this project, the fact that it was innovative, cutting-edge and we were moving into an area which, frankly, in Singapore, we, at that time, did not have much experience in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And also, it was a question of risk allocation, having a PPP project in the way I have described, puts this partner in the context of having some skin in the game.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And to ensure that every delay, every failure of availability, in other words, when the stadium or the facility is not available because of a defect or a problem with the facility, that is a responsibility they bear.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you went to a third party and you bought those services, then the Government will bear the risk of that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Quite apart from that, the Government would also have had to bear the risk and the financial obligation of incurring the capital expenditure (capex) from the start.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, having regard to what I have said earlier, I think I have explained why, whilst we could have in the way Mr Gerald Giam has put it, we chose not to do so in a procurement model but to do it by way of a PPP.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On Mr Gerald Giam's last question whether we want to host all national school games and all other community games there because, as Mr Giam puts it, facilities are block booked and unavailable, we have to be clear.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Sports Hub, obviously, is a top-class infrastructure and you cannot conflate that with training and more local, domestic events for which we have many of the ActiveSG facilities available in the stadium and other facilities around the island.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we got to make sure that the relevant level of facility is used to host and cater for the relevant level of sporting activity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, I did say we do want some national school games to be there – the finals or key moments – but we cannot turn the Sports Hub into a place where every school event is being held there.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Can Mr Gerald Giam please repeat the second question on SportSG?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Yes, my second question was how will SportSG be able to bring in more marquee events when SHPL, with all its international expertise, was not able to?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Well, first of all, that has been done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we have built up our expertise over the years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also worked with developed partners in the private sector today.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I have mentioned UnUsual Limited, LiveNation being here, AEG and so on, located in Singapore, having a vested interest in making sure that they bring these products into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is not just about SportSG, but, as I have said, the maturity and development of the entire ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Gerald Giam's other point I think presupposes that when PPP partner, SHPL, did not bring marquee events into Singapore it is because they were unable to do so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Part of the reason is because the cost structure of the project disincentivised them from doing so on a freely available basis because the cost structure meant that they would have to bear the risk of there, for example, not having a good turnout or good take-up of the ticket sales for such events, then the losses would be borne by them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there were a number of structural problems with the current arrangement, which made it harder, not impossible, but harder for SHPL to have done so.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am very excited to hear about it, especially since the bulk of it falls within my constituency.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But, Sir, Members of Parliament in this House need to hold the Government accountable for Ministries' expenditure.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, I think Liverpool played recently at Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Did the Government take a share in any of these major events?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Because if it does, then we also need to balance how much we will lose in terms of lost revenue in taking over the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In most cases, there is not much that comes down to a level which allows the Government to share and that, itself, is also one of the considerations behind this decision, because if we were to take on board the entire project and run and manage it ourselves, as I mentioned earlier, then we would avail ourselves entirely of the upsides of any of these projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Of course, these are things which we should not automatically assume that just because a team like Liverpool comes here, that there will automatically be a tremendous upside, because you have to weigh up these commercial considerations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the point is, once we take back ownership of this, the structure allows us to then directly manage it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will assess the risk and if it is something we can get into, then the commercial revenue and the upsides can be taken by the Government in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, currently, there is a formula that prescribes the usage and the allocation of these takings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: After we terminate it and we do it on our own, then all of these would be within SportSG and within the Government to control.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Please allow me to have one or two minutes of preamble, before I ask my questions, okay?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Perhaps, I can restrict you to half a minute, please.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: There has been a lot of aspirational delivery throughout this session.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I must also share my experience, that, first, I support the Government taking back the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We are all very attached to the old National Stadium.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Ministers past and present have participated in the opening of the old National Stadium together with me in 1973.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are very attached to the old National Stadium.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We do not know why the Sports Hub was given to a private consortium.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, then, we have to go into a lot of details of financial calculations and all that, but we still need to debate about that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But so far, no question has been raised.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The fact remains why the decision was made at the beginning —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Be fair to the Members who are after you also wanting to ask clarifications.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will give you the leeway, but please keep it short.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The second question is, looking at the financial numbers – and bear with me a little while on that ‒ basically, SHPL seems to have failed in its job, failed in the expectations that we have on them.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, when we ask international companies to come in, I am in business for many years, I know!

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When I use the international partners, we expect them to bring in the marquee events.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If they did not bring in the marquee events, they have failed in their job.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, why, for example, in the compensation formula, do we pay for the $1.2 billion, which, I presume, is the outstanding bank loan?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I have been listening to you quite carefully.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: You have asked your first question quite succinctly.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I invite you to ask your second and final question now succinctly.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I will let the Minister elaborate first then.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think I have spent the better part of the last 45 minutes precisely doing that, elaborating at some length, because I think Mr Leong did ask that question about why we chosed the PPP model.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I thought I had explained in some detail why we considered the procurement model but it was not appropriate, why we wanted to put the risk-sharing allocation mechanism to work, so that our partners would have skin in the game, that they would bear the risk as well, that there will be financial and market discipline in the way we structured the arrangement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think all of this Mr Leong would understand very well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, in the first place, why we went into it, why we chose this model, I think I have explained that in some detail.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The majority of this cost is the capex, as I have explained and this is the capex that we would have had to bear had we undertaken the procurement model anyway.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To give Mr Leong an example, if we had taken the procurement model, we would have had to raise the entire cost of the construction upfront and paid it by around 2010, which was when the project started, even before it became ready.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, a full commitment of the sum in 2010.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And over the years, we would have had to make at least two large payments every year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It goes towards, as I have explained earlier, for SHPL to meet their loan obligations and to meet their expenses for operations, maintenance, lifecycle costs and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Instead of paying the sum upfront, what we did was we asked SHPL to come in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You have heard me explain it earlier, so, I would not go further into it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And they bear the risks and the costs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And once it is ready, and only when it is ready, we then make the payments each year to SHPL.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On that basis, when we take over, these are costs that we would have had to bear anyway, at least for this portion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The rest of it, as I have said, is an open market valuation, because they are the current owners of the asset, and then there are some items like deductions, more minor items, how we deal with the debt reserve account and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, in that regard, I have set out the premise of the payment, the formula by which this is done and why I believe this is a fair assumption.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will come back to you, Mr Leong Mun Wai.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: No, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, it is a continuation.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think there is a point of order, Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We have to give people a chance in the House to ask their clarifications.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The next person the Chair is calling is Ms He Ting Ru.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to follow up on the question that I asked the Minister previously.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I am not sure whether it was answered.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It was whether a review would be held to look into the circumstances that basically led to this early termination of the PPP project.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is really very much in the spirit of taking up learning points to be applied to similar projects in the future, whether it is for a vibrant sports and events scene in Singapore or, in particular, in terms of our negotiation and structuring or usage even of the PPP projects in the future, whether or not there is anything to be learnt from this.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The Minister has described that some parts of the project have been assessed to be successful, but,  other parts have fallen short.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I am just wondering in terms of the learning points, making sure that any mistakes are not being repeated in the future, whether this is something that is going to be taken and whether this review and the results would be shared with the public.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Everything I mentioned in my speech earlier are all factors that we took into account to reach this decision.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, that review actually had been done and that is why we are confident and capable of coming to Parliament and explaining this to Members and embarking on this termination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To Ms He Ting Ru's point about whether all of these learning points would become something that we take on board, obviously, yes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With each PPP project that we do and indeed, for the Government, with each project that we do, large or small, there are always continual learning points.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We look back, we reflect and we think about what we could have done better and take all those learning points into play as we embark on new projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I also want to emphasise that, in this project, it is somewhat unique and different as well, for the reasons I have set out earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And also because, as I have said, this is a multi-year project over two decades, for which at different junctures of this project, there are different objectives.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is why the agreement is structured this way – to put financial discipline, to put technical expertise at the forefront, at the start of the project, but, along the way, to give us the ability to step in to manage when we feel that we were able to do so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that is exactly how this project was done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, obviously, these are learning points that we will take on board and in subsequent projects, whether it is PPP or otherwise, they will feature in the thinking as we embark on this with third parties.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I believe many sportsmen and women and athletes in our national schools feel the excitement on the vision on the integrated sports precinct.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Minister mentioned that sports, such as football, tennis and track and field, would have world-class facilities at the new sports precinct.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we create equal opportunities for other sports, such as floorball, netball and even boxing, to benefit from this vision and investment in our sporting future?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I say this because some in the fraternities, for instance, the netball fraternity, are worried that they have got to move out of their Kallang Netball Centre, a much beloved location with facilities for netball.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not an exhaustive list and there are various other plans in the pipeline.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I mentioned these because you do need something specialised for these sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You need a specialised facility to play tennis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whereas if you have a hall that has a big space, it can be reconfigured for various purposes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As you know, the Indoor Stadium can be reconfigured for basketball.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Floorball has taken place there in the OCBC Arena.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We can also reconfigure it into one that deals with netball competitions as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there are a number of options when you have these spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whereas for cycling, football, tennis and some others, you will need a specialised facility to play that sport.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having said that, the Member's point about netball, I understand that they are moving out because that area is part of the area that, from memory, will be developed into the Youth Hub in time to come.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Netball, we have been in touch with them and will ensure that they will have a place that they are comfortable with and that they will be able to continue training and take care of the national players and their training needs as well.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We will have Mr Leong Mun Wai and we will end with Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But actually I have to be given the right to ask because the Minister did not answer the question.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I am giving you the ability to ask, but not to elaborate in a speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the contractual agreement provides for the way in which the sums are calculated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the $193.7 million is not just for operation and maintenance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: From my memory, the single largest portion of the $193.7 million goes towards debt service.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: One more question and then we will go to the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Can I ask the Minister what is the debt servicing amount inside the $193.7 million?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Deputy Speaker, we have not got to the bottom of the thing.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Well, if you need to, you can file a specific Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: But to be fair to the Members, this is a topical issue —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But what is the point of having the debate without getting to the bottom of the thing, having all kinds of questions?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We must get to the bottom of the issue.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am asking and I do not think —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: It is a point of order, Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I have been very fair to you and the Chair has called Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: But before that, I think Leader of the House would like to have a word.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, I invite you to take your seat, Mr Leong.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this case, Mr Leong Mun Wai had put a couple of questions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I think the fact that Mr Leong does not understand the answer does not mean that the question has not been answered.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because the Leader is accusing me of not understanding certain things.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I invite you to ask Parliamentary Questions, which any Member is capable of doing, if you think that your questions have not been suitably answered by Minister Edwin Tong.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But now, not only my question has not been suitably answered but the Leader is accusing me of something.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I am not sure that the Leader of the House is accusing you —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: She is accusing me that I do not understand the financials behind all the questions I am asking.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am going to say this as a final position to you.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think you have spoken on this issue three or four times in this debate alone and I asked you to give way to the Member whom I have just called, Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In 2014, I asked a Parliamentary Question with regard to non-performance by SHPL.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This was on the back of the Brazil-Japan football game when there were concerns about pitch quality and so forth.
